Get Data

Source: R/functions.R
get_data.Rd

Downloads all pages of data for one or more metrics and combines them into a single table.

Usage

get_data(
  theme = NULL,
  sub_theme = NULL,
  topic = NULL,
  geography_type = NULL,
  geography = NULL,
  metric = NULL,
  save_to = NULL,
  as_data_table = FALSE,
  max_datasets = 500,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

theme

the largest overall topical subgroup of data. For example infectious_disease.

sub_theme

a topical subgroup associated with the parent theme. For example respiratory.

topic

categorical subgroup associated with the selected theme and sub_theme. For example, COVID-19.

geography_type

the overarching area type for the intended geography. For example Nation.

geography

the selected area under the geography_type. For example England.

metric

the type of data being selected. For example COVID-19_testing_PCRcountByDay.

save_to

optional file path. If supplied, the combined result is also written to disk: .rds files with saveRDS(), anything else (e.g. .csv, .csv.gz) with data.table::fwrite().

as_data_table

if TRUE, return a data.table; otherwise (the default) a data.frame.

max_datasets

safety limit on the number of metric datasets a wildcard query may download. Raise it deliberately for very broad queries.

verbose

show progress messages.

Value

           data.frame (or data.table) containing the query
                   results.

Details

Every query argument accepts:

  • a single exact value, e.g. "E-coli";

  • a character vector of values, e.g. c("England", "Wales");

  • "*" to download every available value at that level;

  • a glob pattern using * or ?, e.g. "NHS*London*" or "*PercentResistant*".

Wildcards can be used at any level, including theme and sub_theme. Every matching combination is downloaded and the results are stacked with data.table::rbindlist(). Each row keeps its own theme, topic, geography, metric, etc. columns, so the combined table is self-describing.

Use get_combinations first to see how many datasets a wildcard query will download.

For further information on the UKHSA dashboard API please visit the API documentation.

          If any argument is left \code{NULL} or is invalid,
                   the possible values for that argument are shown as a
                   message and \code{NULL} is returned invisibly.
                   Datasets that fail to download are skipped with a
                   message; the rest are still returned.

Rate limiting

All requests are throttled to getOption("ukhsadatR.requests_per_second", 1) and retried with backoff on HTTP 429/503, so a wildcard query of N datasets takes at least N seconds by default. Lists of available options are cached for the session (see clear_cache). Please keep broad queries proportionate: preview them with get_combinations.

Examples

# \donttest{
get_data(
  theme = "infectious_disease",
  sub_theme = "respiratory",
  topic = "COVID-19",
  geography_type = "Nation",
  geography = "England",
  metric = "COVID-19_cases_casesByDay"
) |>
  head()
#>                theme   sub_theme    topic geography_type geography
#> 1 infectious_disease respiratory COVID-19         Nation   England
#> 2 infectious_disease respiratory COVID-19         Nation   England
#> 3 infectious_disease respiratory COVID-19         Nation   England

#> 5 infectious_disease respiratory COVID-19         Nation   England
#> 6 infectious_disease respiratory COVID-19         Nation   England
#>   geography_code                    metric metric_group stratum sex age year

#> 2      E92000001 COVID-19_cases_casesByDay        cases default all all 2020
#> 3      E92000001 COVID-19_cases_casesByDay        cases default all all 2020
#> 4      E92000001 COVID-19_cases_casesByDay        cases default all all 2020
#> 5      E92000001 COVID-19_cases_casesByDay        cases default all all 2020

#> 5     2       6 2020-02-03           18                     FALSE

# all ICBs, all E. coli resistance metrics, saved as CSV
ecoli <- get_data(
  theme = "infectious_disease",
  sub_theme = "antimicrobial_resistance",
  topic = "E-coli",
  geography_type = "Integrated Care Board",
  geography = "*",
  metric = "*PercentResistant*",
  save_to = file.path(tempdir(), "ecoli_icb.csv")
)
